items.title: HarperCollins is betting big on AI Audiobooks
items.excerpt: HarperCollins is using its ElevenLabs partnership to push AI-generated narration into foreign-language editions and backlist titles that never justified a studio recording. The publisher says human narration stays its standard, while narrator groups warn about synthetic voices displacing professional voice work.

items.title: 'Hard to ignore' – AI speculation sparks debate about whether authors of colour targeted
items.excerpt: A run of authors publicly suspected of using generative AI has triggered a trade-wide debate over whether writers of colour are disproportionately targeted by AI-detection speculation. Agents and publishers say unverifiable accusations are becoming a reputational risk with no reliable adjudication process.

items.title: What the Viral Study of AI in Self-Published Amazon Books Really Sets Out to Do
items.excerpt: Tuhin Chakrabarty's peer-reviewed analysis of 14,419 self-published Amazon titles found signs of AI use in more than 25% of them. Those books sold less than human-written ones but still reached commercially viable revenue, complicating the assumption that readers simply reject AI-assisted work.

items.title: Guest Post — Do we need (r)evolution in peer review?
items.excerpt: A guest post argues the peer-review system is buckling under reviewer shortages while AI reshapes both submissions and reports: AI-drafted manuscripts show measurably worse readability, and review reports increasingly look AI-assisted. It warns that only large publishers can afford AI reviewer assistants, widening the gap with smaller presses.

items.title: News Podcast: Literary Agents Update Ethics Rules; Seven-Figure Deal Shelved Over AI Claims
items.excerpt: Dan Holloway's weekly roundup covers the AALA ethics-code rewrite, a seven-figure book deal shelved over AI allegations, and the new peer-reviewed study of AI-assisted books on Amazon. The through-line is that the trade still has no accepted method for proving how a manuscript was written.

items.title: These new features are coming to the iFlytek AINOTE 2
items.excerpt: iFlytek published a roadmap preview for its AINOTE 2 e-paper writing tablet, detailing AI note-processing upgrades such as categorized bookmarks, structured note insertion and expanded transcription. It is a look at how AI is being wired directly into reading-and-writing hardware rather than a cloud app.

items.title: Links of Interest: August 5, 2026
items.excerpt: Friedman's roundup flags poets discovering their copyrighted work inside Giggle Academy's learning materials, alongside Princeton University Press's AI-licensing partnership. It is a snapshot of how quietly author work keeps surfacing inside AI-fed products.

items.title: From Blog To Community To Book: A Non-Fiction Author's Journey With Suzanne Smith
items.excerpt: Joanna Penn's episode follows a four-year path from niche blog to community to traditionally published book, with an intro segment on how writers stand out in the age of AI. The practical argument: audience and lived expertise are the parts AI drafting cannot supply.

items.title: From Hub to Hustle: The Scattered Social Landscape in Scholarly Comms
items.excerpt: New Pulse Check data shows scholarly communication has fragmented across platforms, with Reddit rising sharply because of its outsized weight in what LLM assistants surface as answers. Publishers are effectively marketing to chatbots as much as to readers.

items.title: News Summary: A Tale of Two Seven-Figure Deals (and the Response to AI Allegations)
items.excerpt: Two seven-figure deals hit AI allegations and produced opposite outcomes — one publisher stood by its author, the other walked away. The contrast shows how much of AI policy in trade publishing is still improvised case by case.

items.title: AI here, there, everywhere
items.excerpt: Books+Publishing's daily briefing surveys how thoroughly AI has spread through the Australian book trade, from production to bookselling to the ongoing rights fights. Body-text date confirmed as Monday, 3 August 2026.

items.title: Applications Still Open for Korea's Asian Publishers Week 2026
items.excerpt: Seoul's Asian Publishers Week (November 3–6) is themed 'Publishing in the Era of AI: Between Crisis and Opportunity,' and is asking attendees to bring practical AI experience from their own markets. Applications remain open.

items.title: AI May Be Making Publishing Easier, But It's Still Not Easy
items.excerpt: At the Publishing Signal Media Transformation Summit, speakers agreed AI has cut production cost and time but left the hard part untouched: deciding what to publish. Takeaways centered on machine-readable metadata, management buy-in, and AI's inability to forecast demand. Byline date read from body text (Jul 31, 2026).

items.title: In the age of generic AI narratives, is dialect fiction the key to capturing readers?
items.excerpt: Writer and academic Dr Jen Bowden argues LLMs still fail at regional voice and dialect, making dialect fiction a craft advantage as machine-smoothed prose spreads. A concrete argument about which parts of writing style remain out of reach.

items.title: 'Genius' novel sold in six- and seven-figure deals at auction pulled over suspected AI use
items.excerpt: A crime novel that had drawn major six- and seven-figure deals in the UK and US was withdrawn by its agent after AI-use allegations. The collapse shows how fast an unverifiable AI suspicion can unwind an acquisition.

items.title: Update on Substack's AI detection using Pangram
items.excerpt: Substack's site-wide Pangram-based AI detection rollout has produced confusion and disputes among writers over false positives and opt-outs. A direct look at what happens when detection labels get attached to published prose by default.

items.title: Boomers Can't Stop Gifting Their Grandkids AI-Generated Slop Books
items.excerpt: Personalized AI picture books built from real photos of children are flooding gift markets, and parents are pushing back on garbled text and uncanny illustration. A close-up on where generated children's publishing actually lands with readers.
